newsitem.title: UK: MED OIL PRODUCTS UNDERPINNED BY TIGHT SUPPLIES.
newsitem.headline: MED OIL PRODUCTS UNDERPINNED BY TIGHT SUPPLIES.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were looking more resistant to recent NWE price falls because of some fundamental tightness.

Gas oil eased $1.50 across the board while physical activity was very quiet. August IPE gas oil, which expires at midday on Tuesday, slid to last trade at $168.00 a tonne. September was $1.25 lower at $169.50.
French quality GOM gas oil eased slightly to offer at around September IPE +$3 with one bid heard around September IPE +$2.
Russian heating oil remains in fairly short supply and is talked at around $2 to $3 over the cif high Med quotations basis Italian islands.
One cargo being loaded by a trading house at Tuapse has yet to find a home, while two cargoes of Russian 0.5 percent gas oil were shown on Monday without result.

High sulphur fuel oil cargoes were said to be fetching strong premiums in the dry Mediterranean market, especially rare bunker spec. Little talk was seen on utility spec, but levels were pegged around $84 fob. A refiner said he was offered to move bunker spec to the Canary Islands at about high cif Med +$6, or around the $100 cif mark, adding he would have to buy in northern Europe due to absence of material in the Med.
"Traders in northern Europe are not willing to move stuff to the Mediterranean due to the price difference so buyers in the Med have to pay higher premiums," he added.
A NWE trader of Russian material confirmed this view, adding: "Selling cargoes into the Med does not work nowadays unless you have extremely cheap shipping rates."

One percent continues to be quiet with the biggest buyer on holiday but there was unconfirmed talk of an independent trader selling some 50,000 tonnes of low sulphur material out of Gothenburg into the Med.
